hook: Nasdaq 100 sank 5.6% in its worst week since Covid, yet Nifty just rallied over 14% in a month

mood.basis: proxy: 0.35 x S&P 500 + 0.15 x avg(Nikkei, Kospi)

stories.title: Nasdaq 100 sinks 5.6% in its worst week since Covid; S&P 500 slips 3.7% into correction
stories.summary: The Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6% this week, its worst week since March 2020, and the S&P 500 slipped 3.7% into correction territory. Investors sold AI and tech stocks on worries about slowing data-center construction, tighter funding for AI projects and weaker technology earnings growth. The selloff could weigh on Indian IT stocks and global risk appetite when markets reopen on Monday.
stories.why: A global tech rout can weigh on Indian IT and sap risk appetite, though FPI buying has so far held up.
takeaways: The selloff came from worries about slower data-centre construction and tighter funding for AI projects.
It is the Nasdaq 100's worst week since March 2020.
Indian IT stocks are the most exposed when markets reopen on Monday.

stories.title: Nifty posts its biggest 4-week rally in 6 years, up over 14% in a month; Bank Nifty hits record
stories.summary: The Nifty posted its fourth straight weekly gain, its biggest four-week rally in six years, rising over 14% in a month. Bank Nifty hit a record high. SBI, Maruti Suzuki, Max Healthcare and Apollo Hospitals were among the key gainers, while mid and small caps lagged behind. The rally has been led mostly by large companies, so breadth is worth watching next week.
stories.why: The rally is narrow and large-cap led, so breadth beyond heavyweights is worth watching.
takeaways: Fourth straight weekly gain for the Nifty; up over 14% in a month.
SBI, Maruti Suzuki, Max Healthcare and Apollo Hospitals led the gains.
Mid and small caps lagged, so the rally rests on large companies.

stories.title: IndusInd Bank posts its biggest single-day gain in over five years, crossing ₹1,000
stories.summary: IndusInd Bank shares had their biggest single-day gain in more than five years as Nifty Bank hit a record high. The stock crossed the ₹1,000 level for the first time since September 9, 2026. It is now 7.8% away from its 52-week high of ₹1,077.85, set on July 22, 2026. The jump shows money rotating back into banks.
stories.why: A sharp rebound in a laggard lender shows how strongly money is rotating into banks.
takeaways: First close above ₹1,000 since September 9, 2026.
Now 7.8% below its 52-week high of ₹1,077.85, set on July 22.
The jump came on the day Nifty Bank hit a record high.

stories.title: Ashoka Buildcon, with SAM India JV, is lowest bidder for ₹2,758 crore Jaipur Metro packages
stories.summary: Ashoka Buildcon, in a joint venture with SAM India, emerged as the lowest bidder for two Jaipur Metro Phase-II packages worth ₹2,758.31 crore including GST. The contracts cover elevated viaducts and 23 stations. With this, the company's recent L-1 positions across metro and highway projects rise to more than ₹4,200 crore. L-1 means lowest bidder, not yet a final award.
stories.why: Fresh infra order visibility supports the construction firm's order book.
takeaways: Two Jaipur Metro Phase-II packages: elevated viaducts and 23 stations.
Recent L-1 positions across metro and highway projects now top ₹4,200 crore.
L-1 means lowest bidder; the contract is not yet awarded.

movers.name: Ashoka Buildcon
movers.why: L-1 bidder on ₹2,758 crore metro packages

stories.title: HDFC Bank shares recover 22% in November, adding ₹2.38 lakh crore in market value
stories.summary: HDFC Bank shares rose 22% in November as easing leadership concerns, better business performance and stronger market sentiment brought investors back. The rally added ₹2.38 lakh crore to its market value, which is now above ₹13 lakh crore. The stock is still down 14% in 2026. Because the bank has a big weight in the indices, its rebound lifts the wider market.
stories.why: HDFC Bank's weight in the indices means its rebound lifts the whole market.
takeaways: Market value is back above ₹13 lakh crore.
Easing leadership concerns and better business performance drew investors back.
The stock is still down 14% in 2026.

stories.title: Canara Bank sees limited stress in its ₹2.8 lakh crore gold loans despite price fall
stories.summary: Canara Bank says its ₹2.8 lakh crore gold loan portfolio is holding up despite a sharp fall in gold prices. Delinquencies are just 0.02% and there have been no gold auctions so far, according to MD and CEO Brajesh Kumar Singh. Its conservative 65% loan-to-value ratio gives a cushion against further price declines, easing worries about lenders with large gold loan books.
stories.why: It eases worries that falling gold prices could hurt lenders with large gold loan books.
takeaways: Gold-loan delinquencies are just 0.02%, with no gold auctions so far.
A 65% loan-to-value ratio leaves a cushion if gold falls further.
The comment came from MD and CEO Brajesh Kumar Singh.

stories.title: Rupee climbs past 93 per dollar for the first time since April as shorts unwind
stories.summary: The Indian rupee strengthened past 93 per dollar for the first time since April. Over $12 billion of foreign investment flowed into Indian equities in November, and hedge funds unwound bearish bets on the rupee. The Reserve Bank of India has also taken steps to support the currency. A stronger rupee eases imported inflation but can squeeze exporters such as IT firms.
stories.why: A firmer rupee eases imported inflation but can squeeze IT exporters' earnings.
takeaways: First time past 93 per dollar since April.
Over $12 billion of foreign money went into Indian shares in November.
Hedge funds unwound bets against the rupee; the RBI also stepped in.

stories.title: Gold logs worst week since March as hawkish Fed signals more rate hikes
stories.summary: Gold slid for a fifth day and logged its biggest weekly decline since March. A hawkish US Federal Reserve signalled more interest-rate hikes, and a rout in AI stocks spurred selling across metals markets. Higher rates make non-yielding gold less attractive. The fall matters for Indian gold lenders and the jewellery trade, which are sensitive to bullion prices.
stories.why: Falling gold hits sentiment for Indian gold lenders and the jewellery trade.
takeaways: Fifth straight day of losses for gold.
A hawkish Fed signalled more rate hikes.
The AI selloff spread to selling across metals markets.

stories.title: FIIs pump in nearly ₹32,700 crore this week, extending buying streak to 15 sessions
stories.summary: Foreign institutional investors bought ₹32,646.67 crore of Indian equities this week, extending their buying streak to 15 sessions. Friday's purchase of ₹10,308 crore was the biggest daily buying of the week. Sustained foreign buying has been a key support behind the Nifty's rally. The next question is whether the flows hold if global markets stay under pressure.
stories.why: Sustained foreign buying has been the main support behind the Nifty's rally.
takeaways: ₹32,646.67 crore of buying this week.
Friday's ₹10,308 crore was the biggest single day of the week.
The buying streak is now 15 sessions long.

stories.title: Rupee could strengthen to 92 per dollar, Kotak Neo says; Reuters poll sees RBI hikes
stories.summary: Kotak Neo's Anindya Banerjee says the rupee could strengthen to 92 per dollar and may test 91 if the RBI does not intervene. A Reuters poll shows the RBI is expected to raise its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December and to 6% in February, as inflation breaches its 6% tolerance limit. Rising energy costs are a concern.
stories.why: Rate hikes and a stronger rupee both matter for banks, importers and exporters.
takeaways: Kotak Neo says the rupee could reach 92 and test 91 if the RBI does not step in.
A Reuters poll expects the repo rate at 5.75% in December and 6% in February.
Inflation has breached the RBI's 6% tolerance limit.

stories.title: Sharp rupee rise may cut IT firms' FY27 earnings by up to 13%, report says
stories.summary: A new report says the sharp rise of the rupee could cut Indian IT firms' FY27 earnings by up to 13%. A stronger rupee hurts because these firms earn mostly in foreign currencies, and the impact is bigger for companies with large European exposure. Traditional cost-saving levers are running out, so protecting profit margins will be harder in the months ahead.
stories.why: A strong rupee squeezes margins of IT exporters.
takeaways: IT firms earn mostly abroad, so a stronger rupee shrinks their rupee earnings.
Companies with large European exposure are hit hardest.
Traditional cost-saving levers are running out.

stories.title: FPIs pour a record ₹1.15 lakh crore into Indian equities so far in November
stories.summary: Foreign portfolio investors put a record ₹1.15 lakh crore into Indian equities so far in November, led by financials and consumer stocks. The buying follows improved earnings, more appealing valuations and easing oil prices. Analysts warn the flows could slow if crude rises or US bond yields increase. That makes oil and global yields the key things to watch from here.
stories.why: Foreign flows are the main support behind the Nifty's rally.
takeaways: Financials and consumer stocks drew most of the money.
Better earnings, cheaper valuations and easing oil prices drove the buying.
Rising crude or US bond yields could slow the flows.

stories.title: Shriram Finance to replace Trent in the 30-stock BSE Sensex from December 21, 2026
stories.summary: Shriram Finance will replace Trent in the 30-stock BSE Sensex, with the change taking effect on December 21, 2026. The BSE 100 will see five additions and five exclusions. Multi Commodity Exchange of India, Vedanta, Laurus Labs, Bharat Heavy Electricals and GE Vernova T&D India will be added, while Punjab National Bank, Godrej Consumer, SRF, Shree Cement and Havells will exit.
stories.why: Index changes trigger buying and selling by funds that track them.
takeaways: The change takes effect on December 21, 2026.
Punjab National Bank, Godrej Consumer Products, SRF, Shree Cement and Havells India leave the BSE 100.
Index funds must buy the stocks entering and sell those leaving.

stories.title: AMD falls 7.72% and slips further after hours as short-seller flags China ties
stories.summary: AMD shares fell 7.72% in Friday's regular session and slipped further after hours. Short-seller Hunterbrook Media questioned the chipmaker's China exposure, alleging that AMD continued providing firmware updates to a Chinese server maker on the US export blacklist. The fall adds to the pressure on chip and AI stocks this week, which can spill over to Indian companies linked to the AI theme.
stories.why: Pressure on chip stocks can spill over to AI-linked Indian names.
takeaways: Short-seller Hunterbrook Media questioned AMD's China exposure.
It alleged firmware updates continued for a Chinese server maker on the US export blacklist.
AMD fell 7.72% in the regular session and slipped further after hours.

stories.title: SEBI proposes scrapping extra disclosure rules for foreign investors
stories.summary: SEBI has proposed scrapping the Additional Disclosure Framework for foreign portfolio investors. It says India's ownership disclosure rules go beyond global norms and create entry barriers. The move follows ₹5.61 lakh crore of FPI equity outflows since October 2024, even as foreign institutions have recently turned buyers for 15 straight sessions. The proposal is open for public comment before any final decision.
stories.why: Easier rules could draw more foreign money into Indian equities.
takeaways: SEBI says India's disclosure rules go beyond global norms and create entry barriers.
FPIs pulled ₹5.61 lakh crore from equities since October 2024.
The proposal is open for public comment before any decision.

stories.title: Foreign investors turn overweight on India for the first time since January 2026: BofA
stories.summary: Foreign investors turned net overweight on Indian equities for the first time since January 2026, according to a Bank of America fund manager survey. Being overweight means holding more India than the benchmark suggests. However, concerns about limited AI opportunities, slow reforms and currency weakness persist. The shift is a positive signal for flows, though it is not guaranteed to last.
stories.why: A shift in global fund positioning supports Indian equity flows.
takeaways: First net overweight on India since January 2026, per Bank of America's survey.
Concerns remain: limited AI opportunities, slow reforms and currency weakness.

stories.title: Gold has fallen as much as 33% from its February 2026 highs; analysts flag rebound levels
stories.summary: Global gold prices have fallen as much as 33% from their February 2026 highs, and domestic gold prices are down around 26% since January. The sell-off has also spread to silver and industrial metals. Analysts at JM Financial and Motilal Oswal have flagged key support levels for a possible rebound. Domestic prices are also influenced by moves in the dollar-rupee rate.
stories.why: Gold-linked lenders and jewellers track bullion closely.
takeaways: Global gold is down as much as 33% from February 2026 highs.
Domestic gold is down about 26% since January.
JM Financial and Motilal Oswal have flagged levels for a possible rebound.

stories.title: ICICI Securities' Pankaj Pandey prefers HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and Bank of Baroda
stories.summary: ICICI Securities' Pankaj Pandey prefers HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and Bank of Baroda among lenders, and advises avoiding gold financiers. He expects falling commodity prices to support margins across cement, consumer durables, infrastructure and automobile companies. His preferred stocks include Shree Cement, JK Cement, Amber Enterprises, Maruti Suzuki and Apollo Tyres. These are one analyst's views, not advice.
stories.why: Shows where one analyst sees opportunity as commodity prices fall.
takeaways: Pankaj Pandey heads retail research at ICICI Securities.
He expects falling commodity prices to help margins in cement, durables, infrastructure and autos.
This is one analyst's view, not a recommendation from Ripple.

stories.title: Nifty Bank gains over 1,000 points to cross 64,000; Axis Bank hits 52-week high
stories.summary: Indian markets staged a sharp recovery after a gap-down start, with the Nifty near 25,700. The Nifty Bank surged over 1,000 points to cross the 64,000 mark, and Axis Bank touched a 52-week high. Max Healthcare, Apollo Hospitals and Tech Mahindra were among the top gainers. The move shows how strongly buyers stepped in on the dip during the session.
stories.why: Banks led the recovery that kept the index afloat.
takeaways: Markets recovered sharply after a gap-down start, with the Nifty near 25,700.
Max Healthcare, Apollo Hospitals and Tech Mahindra led the gains.
Axis Bank hit a 52-week high.

stories.title: Sitharaman holds ninth pre-Budget consultation with housing, urbanisation and culture stakeholders
stories.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the ninth pre-Budget consultation, this time with experts and stakeholders from the housing, urbanisation and culture sectors. It was held in connection with the Union Budget 2027-28, the Finance Ministry said in a post on X. Secretaries of the Department of Economic Affairs and the Department of Urban Development attended, but no details of proposals were shared.
stories.why: Pre-Budget talks hint at the policy areas the government is weighing.
takeaways: The talks were for the Union Budget 2027-28.
Secretaries of Economic Affairs and Urban Development attended.
The ministry gave no details of the proposals made.

stories.title: Reliance Industries promoters buy 4.26 lakh shares worth ₹57.15 crore
stories.summary: Reliance Industries promoters have increased their holdings by buying 4.26 lakh shares worth ₹57.15 crore through open-market transactions. Promoters are the founding group that controls the company. Buying by promoters is often read by investors as a sign of confidence in the business. The report gave no further detail on which promoter entities made the purchases or at what prices.
stories.why: Promoter buying is often read as a sign of confidence.
takeaways: 4.26 lakh shares bought for ₹57.15 crore.
The purchases were made in the open market.

stories.title: India's capital goods market could reach $1.2 trillion by 2047: CII-BCG report
stories.summary: A CII-BCG report says India's capital goods market could expand to between $1 trillion and $1.2 trillion by 2047. Rising investment in data centres, semiconductors, defence and clean energy is expected to drive the growth. Annual capital expenditure across major industries is projected to rise 30% to ₹32 lakh crore by FY27-29. The report is a long-term projection, not a forecast for next quarter.
stories.why: Supports the long-term case for industrial and engineering companies.
takeaways: Data centres, semiconductors, defence and clean energy drive the growth.
Annual capex across major industries is projected to rise 30% to ₹32 lakh crore by FY27-29.

stories.title: SEBI proposes tighter age and tenure limits for exchange chiefs and public interest directors
stories.summary: SEBI has proposed tighter age and tenure limits for top executives and public interest directors at exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories. It has also proposed a board seat for the mutual fund industry's body at repo clearing house ARCL. These are proposals, not final rules. They are likely to go through public comments first, and any changes would apply to the market infrastructure institutions.
stories.why: Governance changes at market institutions shape investor trust.
takeaways: Covers exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories.
SEBI also proposed a board seat for the mutual fund industry body at repo clearing house ARCL.

stories.title: Gold rate on MCX slips below ₹1.25 lakh per 10 gm, nearing ₹1.21 lakh
stories.summary: Gold rates on the MCX slipped below ₹1.25 lakh per 10 gm and came close to ₹1.21 lakh levels. Gold and silver ETF prices fell to 52-week lows as the metals sold off. Experts are debating whether this is an opportunity for investors or whether more pain lies ahead. Investors in gold ETFs have seen the steep correction show up directly in their holdings.
stories.why: Falling bullion hurts gold-linked stocks and ETF holders.
takeaways: Gold and silver ETFs are at 52-week lows.
MCX gold came close to ₹1.21 lakh per 10 grams.
